topology.chain: three validators in the host namespace on 127.0.0.1, JSON-RPC ports [49880, 49881, 49882]
topology.firewall: node namespaces: outgoing only to the relays' port 8443 and 10.231.78.1 JSON-RPC ports, no incoming connection; relay namespaces: incoming only to port 8443, no outgoing connection; host bridge table: every node-to-node frame dropped
topology.files: each namespace process runs with empty read-only tmpfs mounts over the other parties' directories and the run's private files
topology.thermal_guard: pauses and resumes the run and the validators (their process group); the node, relay and forwarder processes run in their own sessions, so a guard resume never continues a process the run paused for a crash window

ran_as_root.note: Only the namespace, firewall and teardown commands, the namespace entry and a SIGCONT/SIGKILL to a paused process's sudo launcher run as root; every node, relay, forwarder and probe process runs as uid 1000 (setpriv) and the run itself runs as uid 1000.

1: no direct path: before the rules each node reaches a listener in another node's namespace; after them every node-to-node connection is dropped both ways, while B still reaches its own listener
a node reaches neither other host services nor the internet, and a relay reaches neither the chain nor a node
no shared file or socket: each node sees the other nodes' directories, the run's private files and the relays' state as empty, and each relay sees neither the nodes nor the other relay
TLS is verified: the relays verify only under the run's CA, which both nodes pin with --relay-ca-file; the system trust store and an unrelated CA refuse them
relay only: every node names both relays for rail and chat, pins the run's CA and names no direct peer and no Messenger packet socket
2: A's copy of m1 is `carried` once relay 2 accepted it, and not yet delivered while B cannot answer
m1 becomes `delivered` only on B's verified kind-2 ack: carried, then delivered later
B's runtime lists m1 and applies it once
B's runtime answers with messages.reply-direct; the reply is sealed to the card B learned in band and becomes `delivered` on A's ack
A's runtime receives the reply once
A's second message m2 is delivered and applied once
9: relay state is copied while relay 2 held A's copy for B and B's delivery ack for A
a large text (98,304 bytes) is carried in one padded frame bucket and delivered, and applied once

nothing readable at the relays: no live relay state, no snapshot taken while a relay held a copy and an ack, and no relay log contains any message text, conversation, Event, Endpoint or device id or the sender Agent id (the control proves the search works)
every decoded frame is exactly its smallest padded bucket, every stored envelope equals 1,373 + F + 4·⌈B/3⌉ with F in 5,394..5,432, and the snapshots' stored envelope sizes match the formula
3: first contact over the relay: B had no contact file of A, admitted A's first frame and learned A's chat card and relay evidence in band from it
4: relay 1 was down for the whole conversation: every copy and ack of it was accepted by relay 2 only
5: an older duplicate (a fresh generation of A's m1 copy, deposited after B applied m2) reaches B's daemon, is answered `duplicate` with a signed ack, relay-acknowledged, and not listed to B's runtime again
B is stopped; A's copy is carried as generation 1 and both relays hold it

after the re-deposit interval (600 s, the test setting the spec allows) A deposits generation 2 with the same ciphertext and fresh evidence, and generation 1 is withdrawn at every relay that held it (404 or 410 afterwards)
B, restarted, receives the retained message once (generation 2 only) and A's copy is delivered
B and then A are stopped with A's copy carried; the run waits until every descriptor either holds of the other has expired (descriptor lifetime 1800 s)
with B's evidence expired, A seals and deposits no new generation of its copy: it holds it pending and deposits one kind-4 evidence request for B instead
descriptor expiry: B receives the retained copy whose frame evidence expired and answers a signed `rejected` ack with descriptor-expired (A is admitted); the copy does not reach B's runtime

mutual staleness: one kind-4 request (A) and one response (B), each carrying its sender's card and fresh evidence, make both views fresh; A retries the copy only with newer evidence and it is delivered and applied once
a stranger's evidence request (C held a pending copy for B and B's evidence expired) gets the relay ack only: no response and no write at B
no kind-4 request is sent to a peer without a pending copy, none is repeated before the re-deposit schedule, and the descriptors each node published during the run sent none
a copy A carried to B (generation 1 at the relays) before B's Agent is revoked
after B's Endpoint delegation is withdrawn on chain, A's runtime answers a new send and refuses it with a revocation code (CheckPeer reads finalized state); no copy is sealed or carried

the copy carried before the revocation is not re-deposited after it: past its re-deposit time A seals no new generation, the copy stays at generation 1, undelivered, and its last code is a revocation code (so the re-deposit was attempted and refused, not merely not scheduled)
7: an oversize payload is refused with `content-too-large` before sealing (the daemon computes the worst-case frame size, 190,464 bytes, before any key is spent): no delivery is journaled
a rail (OFR1) packet sealed to B's chat key is refused and relay-acknowledged, with no daemon call
an agent.packet Event is refused on the relay route (a valid signed packet; the delegation grants agent.packet)
a packet whose sender (C) is not the Event sender of the copy it carries (A) is refused and relay-acknowledged; nothing reaches B's runtime and B sends no ack to C
a kind-2 ack whose packet sender (C) is not the Agent of the signing Endpoint (B) is refused and relay-acknowledged; A's journal is unchanged

a refused stranger: B downloaded C's copy (its envelope id relay-acknowledged at both relays) and refused it; C's in-band card and evidence are not stored (so it was refused, not held), no Messenger file of B names C (its rollback boundary is unchanged), B sent C no ack, and C's delivery stays carried
6: B's serve is killed while its daemon commits the copy: the Event is committed and the envelope is still listed at the relays (no relay ack)
after the restart B finds the same envelope again, answers it `duplicate` and the runtime applies it once
A's daemon is killed while its carrier deposits: the relays accept the envelope after the kill and A's journal never recorded `carried`
after the restart A retries the same generation key and gets `carried` with no new deposit: one envelope, delivered, applied once
8: an observer deposits junk under the public id of A's envelope at relay 1 first; A's deposit there gets 409 and is abandoned at relay 1
the copy is delivered through relay 2
10: `tosctl` sign-to-deposit cost: the per-frame signing time is recorded

not_verified.item: 5 (offline beyond 24 h across a re-deposit, past every locator lifetime)
not_verified.reason: the relay route reads no locator at all, so there is no locator lifetime to outlast; the offline-across-a-re-deposit case is proven live with the test-shortened re-deposit interval (spec section 4 permits 10 min..20 h), and the run never reads a locator on RouteRelay. The >24 h wall-clock duration itself is not reproduced.
proven live with a test-shortened descriptor (MR1_DESCRIPTOR_LIFETIME); the >7-day default lifetime is not waited out.

not_verified.item: quota isolation between chat and task traffic (D2)
not_verified.reason: M-R1 shares the relays between chat and rail; separate chat relays are a production requirement (spec section 7), not shown here.

product gap: an invite can be created (invites.create) and is checked on receipt, but no runtime operation attaches the bearer to an outbound copy (dispatch never sets Message.AdmissionToken), so no route can present one. First contact here is admitted by B's allow-list roster instead; B still learns A's card and evidence in band.

not_verified.item: 7 (a relay frame sealed to the rail key)
not_verified.reason: needs B's rail key card, which OpenFox keeps only inside its private key files; the run reads no key file. The rail packet sealed to the chat key is proven live.

not_verified.item: 7 (an agent.packet Event arriving over the relay)
not_verified.reason: the sender's daemon refuses to compose it on this route (proven live), so a receive-side case needs a hand-built E2EE copy.
V1 has one device per Agent and the publication roster must include it; the Agent revocation case is proven live.

not_verified.item: 5 (evidence pull with the responder offline > 24 h)
not_verified.reason: the request re-deposit is proven only within the run's duration; the 24 h relay TTL is not waited out.

not_verified.item: multi-device over the relay (D3), and M0 freeze evidence
not_verified.reason: V1 is one Messenger device per Agent; M0 freeze (independent review and a second E2EE implementation) is out of scope.
